definitions.explanation: The state of lacking convenience or being restricted in some way.
A physical limitation or handicap affecting a part of the body.

examples.japanese: {言葉|ことば}が{通|つう}じなくて{不自由|ふじゆう}した。
examples.english: I was inconvenienced because the language didn't get through.

examples.japanese: {生活|せいかつ}には{不自由|ふじゆう}していません。
examples.english: I'm not wanting for anything in daily life.
examples.notes: 不自由しない = to not lack, to want for nothing

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}では{日本語|にほんご}が{通|つう}じず{不自由|ふじゆう}なことが{多|おお}かったが、だんだん{慣|な}れてきた。
examples.english: Overseas, Japanese wasn't understood and there were many inconveniences, but I gradually got used to it.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}が{不自由|ふじゆう}な{方|かた}のための{席|せき}です。
examples.english: This seat is for people with difficulty walking.
examples.notes: Polite way to refer to physical disability

examples.japanese: {目|め}が{不自由|ふじゆう}な{人|ひと}のために、{点字|てんじ}のメニューを{用意|ようい}しています。
examples.english: We have Braille menus available for people with visual impairments.

examples.japanese: {体|からだ}が{不自由|ふじゆう}でも、{周|まわ}りの{助|たす}けがあれば{不自由|ふじゆう}なく{暮|く}らせる。
examples.english: Even with a physical disability, one can live comfortably with help from those around them.
examples.notes: 不自由なく暮らす = to live without inconvenience

notes:
USAGE: {不自由|ふじゆう} is used both for general inconvenience and as a polite term for physical disability.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{不自由|ふじゆう}する (to be inconvenienced, to lack)
・{不自由|ふじゆう}しない (to not lack anything)
・{足|あし}が{不自由|ふじゆう} (difficulty walking)
・{目|め}が{不自由|ふじゆう} (vision impairment)
・{耳|みみ}が{不自由|ふじゆう} (hearing impairment)
・{不自由|ふじゆう}なく{暮|く}らす (to live comfortably)

ANTONYM: {自由|じゆう} (freedom, convenience)
